title: Unit – 3 : Session – 9 : SLO – 2  |  Identify Components — Model, View, Controller
sections: 1. Model — it maintains the application data and business logic.
2. Model — a class with getValue()/setValue()/updateData() methods manages state, so it is the Model.
3. View — the View defines how the user sees and interacts with the application.
4. View — the Model should never reference or update the View directly; changes flow back via the Controller/observers.
1. FALSE — the View only presents data; updating business data is the Model's responsibility (via the Controller).
2. TRUE — the Controller receives user input, processes it and delegates changes to the Model.
1. B — an ActionListener is event-handling logic, which belongs to the Controller.
2. B — a JLabel displaying a name is pure presentation, i.e. the View.
1. Identify the component: B — UserData only stores and exposes data (name getter/setter), so it is the Model.
2. Identify the role: B — ButtonHandler reacts to an event, updates the Model and refreshes the View, so it is the Controller.
